lines.title: This is pi-account-guard. Rotate accounts freely, and never send a turn into the wrong zone.
lines.intro: Many of us keep a work subscription and a personal one in the same pi. Here, pi is open in a personal repository, but the selected model charges the work account. The footer already warns about it.
lines.block-ask: Let's ask for a summary of the garden beds.
lines.block: Before anything is sent, pi-account-guard checks the account against this place. The account, acme, is tagged work. This repository is personal. So the turn is blocked, and nothing reaches the work subscription.
lines.switch-offer: The fix is one keystroke away. The first choice switches to homelab, a personal account.
lines.switch-done: The same prompt runs again on homelab, and the footer shows a match.
lines.tag-intro: Accounts start untagged. Let's switch to spare, an account the guard has never seen, and ask about watering.
lines.tag-prompt: Before the turn goes, the guard asks which zones spare belongs to. Nothing is ticked for you.
lines.tag-done: We tick personal. The turn goes at once, and the tag is saved for next time.
lines.rotate-intro: Rotators and routers switch accounts on their own, sometimes in the middle of a turn. Let's start a longer answer, then switch to the work account while it streams.
lines.rotate-block: The guard catches the change and stops the turn at once. It is aborted, not finished on the work account.
lines.rotate-offer: Once pi is idle, the account it was on comes first. There is no allow once here, because the aborted turn is gone. We switch back to spare.
lines.status-place: Finally, slash guard shows what the guard sees. This directory matches no place rule, so it falls to the default zone, personal.
lines.status-account: Spare is tagged personal, so it matches, and turns here go through.
lines.end: To install it, run the command on screen. Then try slash guard tour, or add your first place rule.
